children: The U.S. will likely delay announcing new tariffs on China and other countries until after the summit between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping next week,
reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
The Trump administration previously planned to release a trade report on alleged excess capacity before the meeting, which would've recommended a 7.5% tariff on Chinese goods.
It's unclear why the report is being delayed and whether the final tariff rate will go beyond 20%, the cap that Washington agreed to during earlier trade talks.
U.S. and Chinese negotiators are scheduled to meet this weekend to discuss any agreements ahead of Xi's state visit.
"A key question for the U.S. team is how much it might be willing and able to leverage tariff threats to push China for stronger import and export commitments," said Nicole Gorton-Caratelli, a
economist. "Chinese exporters' resilience to Washington's hefty tariffs through 2025 is likely to blunt that leverage."
Besides trade, U.S. and Chinese officials are also expected to discuss the Iran war and AI safety risks.

title: U.S. likely to delay new tariffs until after Trump-Xi summit - report
